---
title: "Lesson 1: Manifolds"
---

## Definition

A <u>manifold</u> is a topological space
that locally resembles Euclidean space near any point.

**More precisely:**\
An $n$-dimensional manifold ($n$-manifold) $M$ is a topological space
with the property that each point on $M$ has a neighbourhood
that is topologically isomorphic (homeomorphic)
to an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

## Intuition

The idea is that a curved surface,
such as a sphere, can be studied using coordinate patches.
Near each point, the surface behaves like a flat plane.

## Charts, atlases and local coordinates

A <u>chart</u> is a map $\phi$ from $U$ to $V$

Here, $U$ is an open subset of $M$
and $V$ is an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ (Euclidean space)
$\phi$ is then (by the definition of a manifold) a bijection
from $U$ to $V$, and can be called a <u>chart</u> at $U$

Formally:

$$
\phi: U \subseteq M \longrightarrow V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n
$$
